note: Growth controls (D-88). Every knob the town's shape depends on lives here, basic at start, so a later release can hand growth and zoning to the residents without a schema event. Changing a value here and re-running scripts/derive-plots.mjs is the whole procedure.
districtSizeDerivation: MEASURED, not picked. The floor is ceil(population / RESIDENCE_OCCUPANCY_TARGET_AGENTS) = ceil(85/7) = 13 housing plots (residences.mjs). The 48x46 district packs SIX at the smallest real house footprint and ZERO at any full-size one — the plan's ~25-30 ceiling assumed a 6x5 parcel and omitted the 718 tiles the five existing buildings occupy, which is more than half the 1395 free. 92x92 is the smallest square that packs the TOP of the ruled scarcity band (1.4 -> 19 housing plots) plus all six civic archetypes including the 24x23 school, at the real declared exteriors with a one-tile walkable margin. Sizing to the top of the band means scarcityRatio can move anywhere inside 1.2-1.4 without re-sizing the map.
scarcityRatioNote: The knob, recorded as a RATIO rather than an integer because a bare count hides which end of the constraint moved. plots = ceil(scarcity_ratio * floor). At 1.0 there is zero slack and one hoarded plot is instantly fatal; above ~1.4 the district has no room left for the civic set. 1.3 -> ceil(1.3 * 13) = 17 housing plots.
plotSizeClassesNote: Sizes come from the REAL declared exteriors named in contract/buildings.json (D-88), not from round numbers, and every one of them is an exterior a BUILDING ROW actually references: S is mobile_home_small (6x6); M is terraced_house_1 (12x15), the `house` archetype's own exterior, and therefore also clears villa (9x13), condo_9 (6x12), market (7x12), post_office (8x13) and museum (7x13); L clears country_house (18x16), condo_6 (13x16) and one_story_house (16x14); XL clears the school (24x23). M was 10x15 in the first derivation, sized against terraced_house_modular — art no building row names — so seven housing plots admitted no house at all. The housing counts sum to 17 = ceil(1.3 * 13). What each plot ADMITS is never listed here — scripts/derive-plots.mjs computes it from footprint fit against contract/buildings.json (D-66: physics constrains, law regulates; there is no zone field).
maxDoorAnchorDistanceNote: How far a plot's door may sit from the road/sidewalk network. The grown region has no roads of its own — cityGrid draws one cross, whose arms extend as the grid grows — so parcels out in the new quarters are genuinely far from pavement. The packer places every class nearest-the-street first, so this bound is the MEASURED worst case (51 tiles, plot mean 13) rather than a budget anyone is spending. It is a quality metric, not a reachability one: open grass is walkable, so a far anchor is a long walk past no pavement, never a blocked door — the assertion that matters, and is enforced, is that no anchor sits inside a collision box. extending the road grid into the grown region is the follow-up that shrinks it, and is config-driven like everything else here (D-88).
walkableMarginNote: Kept clear around every plot so the town does not pack itself into a solid block with no way between the parcels.
